newsitem.title: USA: First Union sees capital markets growing.
newsitem.headline: First Union sees capital markets growing.

text.p: First Union Corp intends to keep building its capital markets business but does not feel compelled to make an acquisition, Chief Financial Officer Robert Atwood said in a conference call Thursday.
"We are expanding our own underwriting activities...(but we) don't necessarily feel compelled to have to go out and acquire another institution in order to do that," Atwood said.

Atwood also said First Union is "very comfortable" with previous targets of a 27 percent earnings growth rate in both capital markets and capital management. He noted the company was exceeding those targets currently.

Also speaking to reporters on the conference call was Mal Murray, First Union's chief credit officer. In response to a question, he said the chargeoff rate on the managed credit card portfolio was 7.73 percent in the second quarter compared to 7.26 percent in the first quarter of 1997 and 5.79 percent a year ago. He noted that as part of the company's strategy, the card portfolio is not growing, which results in a "lag effect" that can push the chargeoff rate higher.
Atwood noted that credit card are only about six percent of all loans at First Union.
Atwood said First Union is "very comfortable" that overall loan chargeoffs for the year will be in the range of 50 to 65 basis points, a previously announced target.
In First Union's second-quarter earnings release earlier Thursday, the overall chargeoff rate was 68 basis points.
The provision for loan losses in the second quarter was $165 million, compared to $80 million a year ago. Murray said the increase mostly reflected credit cards.
